channel.title: Travelytix
channel.description: Practical, data-driven travel planning for US and Canadian travelers heading to Mexico and the Caribbean.

item.title: Sargassum this week: how to check your beach before you go
item.description: 96 of 140 monitored beaches in Quintana Roo were at the low level on Nov. 11. Three free tools to check sargassum before booking or heading to the beach.

item.title: Is Cancún safe? What Canada's latest travel advice says and how to stay smart
item.description: Canada's government advises a high degree of caution for Mexico overall; Quintana Roo is not on its avoid-travel list. Practical tips from the official advice, updated Nov. 18, 2026.

item.title: Mexico's tourist fees in USD and CAD: DNR and Visitax explained
item.description: The non-resident fee rises to 1,158 pesos in 2027 (about US$63 / C$91), usually in your ticket. Quintana Roo's Visitax is 293 pesos (about US$16 / C$23), paid online.

item.title: Mexico entry requirements for U.S. and Canadian travelers (2026)
item.description: Passport, no visa for tourism up to 180 days, e-gates for e-passport holders and a digital FMM. What Americans and Canadians need to enter Mexico by air.

item.title: Spending Thanksgiving in Cancún? Here's what to expect this week
item.description: Cancún is the top international Thanksgiving pick for Americans. Hotels ran about 73% full last week, sargassum is low and hurricane season ends Sunday. A quick checklist.

item.title: Cruising from Puerto Vallarta: what US and Canadian travelers should know about Mexico's first home port
item.description: Puerto Vallarta will become Mexico's first cruise home port, where voyages start and end. What's confirmed, what isn't, and how to plan a fly-and-cruise trip from the US or Canada.
